entries.note: 打 can mean to make or perform an action, as it does here.
Often used as a familiar or scolding way to address a boy or young man.

entries.teach: 消 can mean to pass time. Learn this food word together, used for something eaten late at night.
This introduces the one condition that could change a result. It often pairs with 才 or 否則.

Also a respectful way to address an older married woman.

entries.lit: shoes you can slide along in

entries.teach: This describes a favorable opinion of someone. Its opposite is 看不起, which expresses contempt.

entries.note: Used for the greater part of a group, or for what is likely to happen.
時 usually means time. Doubled as 時時, or with 常, it means often.

entries.teach: Used of a friendship between people, often with 很 or 最. 好 here concerns their relationship, rather than a wish for something good.

entries.note: 通 can mean to communicate or connect, as well as to go through.
心 can refer to attention and thought, not just the heart.
氣 can refer to temperament or spirit, as well as air.
好 is pronounced hào here. As a verb it means to be fond of something.
鼓 can mean to rouse or stir up, not just a drum.
提 can mean to bring something up for attention, not only to carry it.
和 here means harmony, not and.
長 can describe what someone excels at. 處 here is an aspect rather than a physical place.

entries.teach: 信 here concerns trust rather than letters. Learn this word together for how reliably someone honors commitments, including financial ones.

entries.note: 上 before a large number can mean to reach that scale.
The different hearts and intentions express a divided mind rather than a firm decision.
口 can mean an opening, not just a mouth.
戶 means door or household, and also an account, as in 帳戶.

entries.lit: a machine for drawing a number
a cabinet with a working surface

entries.note: 身 can mean the person. 分 is pronounced fèn here and refers to status, not minutes.
格 can mean a box or cell in a table, not just a standard.
頭 is a place ending here, as in 裡頭. It does not refer to a head.
現 here describes what is available now, rather than a promise of later payment.
行 is pronounced háng here and refers to a bank.
美 is short for 美國.
裝 here means clothing or dress, as in 服裝.
據 here means evidence or proof, as in 證據.
戶 refers to an account here, rather than a door or household.
印 and 章 can both name a stamp used to leave an identifying mark.
易 can mean to exchange, as in 貿易. Here it does not mean easy.
糊 can mean blurred or unclear, as in 模糊, not just paste.
支 can mean to pay out money, as in 支出. It is not a counting word here.

entries.teach: Both are old words for spans of years. Together they now name the fixed unit of one hundred years.

entries.lit: grouped and woven into a whole

entries.note: 卡 copies the sound of card here. 刷 describes swiping it, though payment can also involve tapping or inserting it.
正 here indicates the main or front side, rather than right now.
帶 can mean a strip, belt, or tape. It does not mean to bring here.
發 can describe unfolding or emerging. 展 here means to expand, rather than an exhibition.
息 usually means breath or rest. In money words it means interest.
本 can mean a copy or edition, not just a root or a counting word for books.

entries.lit: the fewest, setting a lower limit
the most, setting an upper limit

entries.teach: Both characters concern calculating. In use, this judges whether the benefit justifies the money or effort spent.
entries.note: 划 can refer to reckoning costs here, rather than rowing a boat.
子 only rounds the word out here. It does not mean child.
方 can mean square, not just a side or direction.
正 indicates a regular shape. 方 here means square.
尺 and 寸 are traditional Chinese length units. 寸 is one tenth of a 尺, rather than an English inch.
省 means to spare yourself something, as in 省事. What follows 省得 is the trouble you are spared.

entries.lit: a whole day through to evening

entries.note: 目 here means an item or heading, not an eye.
結 can mean to settle or conclude something, not just to tie it.
會 means a club or association here, not can.

entries.lit: enter a name in a register

entries.note: After a verb, 住 can indicate holding something firmly in place. It does not mean to live here.

entries.teach: 活 strengthens 該 here, so the word says the person really had it coming. It can sound harsh, so take care saying it to someone.

entries.lit: not reach the point of needing to use

entries.lit: can find a use for it
entries.note: 得 marks possibility. 著 is pronounced zháo and marks reaching a result, rather than continuing an action.
Repeating 看 makes the action brief or tentative. Here it suggests observing how things turn out before deciding.
面 can refer to the face or front of something. This word can also refer to the shop premises.
本 can mean the money invested in a business, not just a root or book.
折 can mean to reduce a price, not just to break something off.
花 can mean to spend money or time. It does not mean flower here.
下 can mean to issue or place something, such as an order. It does not mean under here.

entries.lit: a checkpoint for goods crossing borders
entries.note: 關 can mean a checkpoint or border pass. This word also applies at airports and land borders.
家 can identify a person or business engaged in an activity. It does not mean home here.
家 can identify a person or business engaged in an activity. It does not mean home here.

entries.lit: the gain does not make up for the loss

得 here means to obtain, rather than marking a complement.

entries.lit: right at the start of the morning

entries.teach: The time and care spent doing something. 夫 only completes the word here. Read it gōngfu.

entries.note: 新 stands for new people here, such as students joining a school.
會 here is a gathering, rather than being able to do something.
手 means hand, and by extension a skill of the hands.
自 means by itself here. The water arrives through pipes without being carried.

entries.teach: Put this fixed expression at the end to limit what you have just said. 已 has the older sense of stopping here.

entries.note: 氣 usually means air. It can also mean the smell something gives off.
中 is short for 中國 here.

entries.teach: Short for 落花生. After flowering, the plant sends a stalk into the soil, where its pods grow. Learn the shortened plant name together.

entries.note: 子 means seed here, rather than child or a noun ending.
麥 names a group of cereal grains. Compare 大麥, barley.
The warm air also names the equipment or system that supplies it.
消 here describes breaking food down, rather than simply disappearing.

entries.lit: generous portions of fish and meat

entries.note: 口 can mean an opening or port. Here goods enter a country through one.
起來 after this verb introduces the result of considering something, rather than physical movement upward.
好 is pronounced hào here and means to be fond of something.
長 is pronounced zhǎng here and means to grow, rather than long.

entries.lit: the seasonal conditions of the air
entries.note: 候 here concerns seasonal conditions, rather than waiting.

entries.lit: the tools for circles and square corners
entries.note: Work done with compass and square comes out correct, so the two tools came to mean rules and proper behaviour.

entries.lit: another point outside what was mentioned

entries.note: 頭 is a noun ending here, rather than a head.

entries.teach: The two characters are used only together and have no meaning apart. Learn 玻璃 as one piece.

entries.note: 分 is pronounced fēn here and means to divide, rather than a minute.

entries.lit: following the natural movement of your hand

entries.note: 浪 here means without restraint, rather than a wave.
生 here means life, rather than being born.
光 means only here, rather than light or completely gone.
果 means result here, extending the idea of fruit as what something produces.

entries.teach: This fixed expression criticizes excessive fussing or hesitation. It uses a stereotype about older women and mothers, rather than describing actual family members.

entries.note: 布 here means to spread information, rather than cloth.

entries.lit: to reduce something and make it lighter
the study of changes in substances
an electric tube held in the hand

單 means a sheet of fabric here, rather than single or a list.
被 is bedding here, rather than the grammar marker for something done to someone.
花 here refers to the fluffy cotton harvested from the plant, rather than its petals.
帶 is a strip or band here, rather than the verb to bring.

entries.teach: Read literally it is "atom pen". It is simply the usual name for a ballpoint pen in Taiwan. Learn it as one piece.

entries.note: 膠 can refer to resin as well as glue.
金 means metal here, and 屬 means a category rather than the verb to belong.
子 only rounds the word out here. It does not mean child.
子 only rounds the word out here. It does not mean child.

entries.lit: the first day of the year
entries.note: 元 means first or beginning here, rather than a unit of money.
院 here names an institution and its building, rather than just a courtyard.
門 can mean a field of activity, rather than a physical door.
念 here means to think of someone or something, rather than to read aloud.

entries.lit: the actual place where something is happening

entries.note: 鼓 can be a verb meaning to beat, as when playing a drum.
不住 after a verb means being unable to maintain control or hold something steady, rather than not living somewhere.
擺 here means to swing back and forth, rather than to arrange.

entries.lit: to let something pass without meeting it

entries.lit: a ticket to go through the entrance

entries.note: 提 can mean bringing a time forward, rather than carrying an object.
精 describes excellence here. 彩 extends from color to splendor.
傷 describes mental strain here, rather than a physical wound.

entries.teach: The expression refers to thinking ability, rather than literal sinews. Use it when talking about solving problems or using your head.
A cry of surprise or dismay. The characters only write the sound.

entries.lit: the person doing the main singing

entries.note: 京 is short for 北京 here.
寧 expresses a preference here, rather than peace.

entries.lit: to find one choice more acceptable
entries.note: 寧 expresses a preference here, rather than peace. 可 expresses acceptability.

轉 means passing a transmission onward here, rather than physically turning.
臺 here means a broadcasting station, rather than a raised platform.
臺 here means a broadcasting station, rather than a raised platform.
從 here means to undertake or pursue, rather than from.
重 here means to give something importance, rather than physical weight.

entries.teach: Learn this as a hospital term. Patients come for a consultation and go home rather than staying in a hospital bed.

entries.note: 假 is jià for time off. The reading jiǎ means false.
社 can name an organization or business, as well as a community.

entries.lit: the place you aim to reach

entries.note: 正 can mean exactly, as well as right.

entries.lit: an image imprinted in the mind
entries.note: 象 means an image or appearance here, not an elephant.
通 has a sense of general or common here, rather than going through.

entries.lit: looking at the splendour of a place
entries.note: 光 can refer to splendour, as well as light.

entries.lit: to test something through personal involvement
entries.note: 體 extends from the body to doing something personally.
自然 can name the natural world as well as describe something as natural.

entries.lit: falling water like a sheet of cloth

entries.note: 班 can refer to a scheduled transport service. 機 is short for 飛機 here.

點 is short for 點心 here, not a clock time.

entries.lit: cloth with a soft raised surface

entries.note: 頭 helps name a place here. It does not mean a head or necessarily the end of a street.

entries.lit: instead, the other option would be better

entries.lit: to get your body moving on a journey

受 means bearing or enduring a feeling here, rather than simply receiving something.

entries.lit: the larger upper part of the leg
a body part with a particular function

entries.teach: Learn the pair as one exclamation. It can express pain, surprise, or alarm, with the tone of voice showing the feeling.

entries.note: 得 is a neutral ending here, not the particle introducing a description of how well something is done.

entries.teach: Literally a vase for flowers. Applied to a person, it dismisses them as decorative rather than capable, so it can be insulting.

entries.note: 皂 alone already means soap, as in 香皂.

性 refers to sex here, rather than temperament or character.
性 refers to sex here, rather than temperament or character.

entries.lit: to regard something as being something else

entries.note: 壓 is short for 壓力 here and refers to mental pressure.
除 is the verb remove here, not the expression meaning except.

entries.teach: Learn this pair as a question signal. It usually challenges an idea or expresses disbelief rather than asking neutrally for information.
entries.note: 道 can mean to say, as well as a road or way.
下 is the verb used for playing chess and similar board games.
果 can mean indeed or really. It does not refer to fruit here.

entries.lit: drawings made with freedom of expression
entries.note: 漫 can mean free or unrestrained, as well as overflowing. The word covers both comic strips and longer illustrated stories.
痛 can intensify an action or feeling, rather than mean pain. 快 has its sense of gladness here.

entries.lit: to force yourself to make an effort
entries.note: 強 is qiǎng here and means forcing, not being strong. The word can also describe barely managing something.

entries.lit: steal free time from a busy day

entries.note: 放 can mean releasing your hold. The expression also applies to allowing someone to act independently.
門 can refer to a field of study or activity, not just a physical door.

entries.lit: respectfully entrusting someone with a request

entries.note: 好 is hào here, meaning to be fond of something, not hǎo meaning good.

entries.lit: to be selected through an exam
entries.note: 取 refers to selection for a place here, rather than fetching an object.
明 can mean clear or evident, as well as bright.

父 forms a respectful family title here. The whole title can also respectfully address a man of your parents’ generation.

entries.lit: the wife of your father's older brother
entries.note: 母 forms a respectful family title here. The whole title can also respectfully address a woman of your parents’ generation.
支 is a verb meaning to prop something up here, not a counting word.
Face refers to dignity or social standing here.

entries.lit: to put your heart to work over something
entries.note: 操 can mean managing or handling something. 心 refers to mental concerns here.

entries.lit: the mark you aim your eyes at

entries.note: 命 can mean giving a command, as well as life or fate.

誇 can mean praising, not only exaggerating. 獎 is a verb here, rather than a prize.

The clause after this pair names an unwanted result you are trying to prevent.
士 is a respectful term for a person here. The word is also a polite title after a surname.
子 and 女 name sons and daughters here, rather than children in general and female.
為 is wéi here and means to be or serve as, not wèi meaning for.
何 can ask why, as well as what. This question suggests that an action is unnecessary.

entries.teach: 價 points to a price, but learn the pair together. It often names effort, loss, or sacrifice involved in getting something.

entries.lit: to change something so it is right

美 usually means beautiful. Here it is a verb, to speak well of.
斷 can mean deciding or settling a matter, as well as breaking something off.

對 means toward or facing here, rather than correct.

倒 here means falling down, not pouring a liquid.

師 can name a skilled professional, not only a classroom teacher.

entries.lit: so intense it could demand your life

entries.note: This can describe social contact generally. For a romantic couple, it refers to their relationship.

entries.note: 典 can mean established rules, and 禮 can mean ritual rather than a gift.
光 here conveys honor. 臨 can refer to arriving at a place.

entries.note: 登 here means entering information in a register, rather than climbing.
